mainEntity.name: How long is a sleep cycle?

acceptedAnswer.text: About 90 minutes on average, moving through light sleep, deep sleep and REM. Individual cycles vary from about 70 to 120 minutes, and the mix shifts through the night.

mainEntity.name: How many hours of sleep do I need?

acceptedAnswer.text: The National Sleep Foundation recommends 7 to 9 hours for adults aged 18 to 64, 8 to 10 for teens, and 7 to 8 for adults 65 and over.

mainEntity.name: Why do I wake up tired after 8 hours?

acceptedAnswer.text: Waking during deep sleep causes sleep inertia, a heavy groggy feeling that can last for a while. Shifting the time by 15 to 30 minutes can change how you feel.

mainEntity.name: What is the best length for a nap?

acceptedAnswer.text: A 10 to 20 minute nap gives an alertness boost with little grogginess. A 90-minute nap is a full cycle. Around 30 to 60 minutes often means waking from deep sleep.

mainEntity.name: Why include time to fall asleep?

acceptedAnswer.text: Cycles only start once you are asleep. If you take 15 minutes to drift off, you need to be in bed 15 minutes earlier to get the same amount of sleep.
